question: Should explicit, run-ID-scoped requester consumption count as terminal descendant delivery even when the requester’s later outward send fails?
rationale: The code can implement either boundary safely, but choosing whether requester consumption or final outward visibility ends descendant retry is a product lifecycle decision that changes message-delivery and session-state semantics.

options.title: Accept requester consumption
options.body: Treat exact requester consumption as terminal descendant delivery after the contributor supplies runtime and restart proof for consumed and unconsumed rows.

options.title: Require outward delivery
options.body: Keep descendants retryable until the requester result is visibly delivered, and adjust the credit call site and tests accordingly.

options.title: Use durable inbox semantics
options.body: Pause this patch and solve consumption, retries, and restart recovery through the broader durable completion inbox tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/67777.

recommendation.title: Accept requester consumption
recommendation.body: Treat exact requester consumption as terminal descendant delivery after the contributor supplies runtime and restart proof for consumed and unconsumed rows.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most directly connects this person to the recent central cron, lifecycle, and SQLite implementation surfaces affected by the choice.
